item.title: Economy loses 92,000 jobs in February
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the economy lost 92,000 jobs in February while unemployment held steady at 4.4%, a development that could spur the Federal Reserve to question whether interest rates are truly in balance.

item.title: Stripe advances security for agentic commerce
item.description: Stripe has expanded its Shared Payment Tokens, a foundational building block to protect agentic commerce, to work with Visa and Mastercard's tokens. It's also added Affirm and Klarna.

item.title: How B2B payment automation threatens banks
item.description: Fintechs and the technology behind cryptocurrency are becoming popular, putting trillions in transaction value at risk for banks, according to Accenture.

item.title: Iran war forces Navy Federal to close Middle East branches
item.description: The credit union closed three of its overseas locations in response to the conflict. Military-focused financial institutions are instead offering digital banking to deployed service members.

item.title: Oil prices may keep inflation elevated, bank economists say
item.description: Chief economists at large and regional banks predicted ongoing inflation, in part because of the anticipated surge in oil prices as a result of the Iran war. The forecast from the American Bankers Association's Economic Advisory Committee did not account for the disappointing U.S. jobs report on Friday.

item.title: JPMorgan's Porretti departs, Goldman bankers pose for fashion shoot
item.description: JPMorganChase's Alfredo Porretti has left the firm; two junior Goldman Sachs bankers took part in a controversial fashion shoot; Societe Generale appointed Selina Cheung head of equity capital markets in Asia Pacific; and more in this week's banking news roundup.

item.title: Western Alliance sues Jefferies for $126M in First Brands fallout
item.description: The Phoenix-based bank said that affiliates of Jefferies had stayed current on the loan agreement until last week. The suit is the latest example of private credit-related problems at banks.

item.title: LexisNexis hit by second data breach in two years
item.description: Cybercriminals say they stole sensitive records by exploiting an unpatched vulnerability known as React2Shell and using the password Lexis1234.

item.title: Fed watchers say discount window revamp overdue — but tricky
item.description: Industry stakeholders say the Federal Reserve's renewed focus on reforming the discount window — the central bank's 'lender of last resort' facility — is welcome. But replacing the system with one that works better is easier said than done.

item.title: Zerohash is latest crypto firm to apply for a trust charter
item.description: The digital asset company, currently partnered with firms like Morgan Stanley and One Pay, is seeking its own national trust bank charter from the OCC.
